sources.entry: Stash - A web-based library organizer and player for your adult media stash, with auto-tagging and metadata scraping support. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: Stash is a self-hosted Go web app that organizes, tags, and serves a local collection of video and image files, with metadata scraping from online sources.
summary.what_it_does: Stash indexes media directories you configure and provides a web interface for browsing, curating, editing, and tagging videos and images. It pulls metadata such as performers, tags, descriptions, and studios from sources including StashDB, other stash-box databases, and community-maintained scrapers that can be installed from within the app. It supports a wide variety of video and image formats and provides statistics about performers, tags, studios and more. Extensibility comes through community-built plugins and themes. The README mentions Docker, Windows, macOS, and Linux as install options, and it requires FFmpeg, which the app can download during setup if missing.
use_cases: scrape performer and studio info into a library
browse and manage personal image and video files
self-host a media library web interface
how_to_run: Install via the Windows, macOS, Linux, or Docker options described in the README (step-by-step instructions at docs.stashapp.cc/installation)
Docker: follow the instructions and sample docker-compose.yml linked in the README
On first run, configure options and pick media directories to scan
Install FFmpeg via your package manager (recommended on Linux), or let Stash download a copy during setup
notable: Metadata scraping from StashDB, other stash-box instances, and community scrapers installable in-app
Extensible through community-built plugins and themes
Supports SFW and NSFW content collections
Built-in statistics on performers, tags, and studios
caveats: Windows requires Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later as of version 0.27.0
macOS requires macOS 12 Monterey or later as of version 0.32.0; older versions can run through Docker
Windows and macOS builds are unsigned, so security prompts appear on first run
